memo.verdict: Park at Triaging with working-hypothesis conviction. Do not progress to Early-Stage Assessment, and do not treat the low multiple as a reason to progress. Retest at the FY26 results in early 2027, when management delivers its first formal Horizon 2030 progress report. Progress only if two of three named tests clear: European exchange-traded-product share at or above 27% with sequential quarterly gains; annualised return on trading capital above 60% across two consecutive quarters; fixed operating expenses landing inside EUR 235m to 245m with FY27 guidance below EUR 250m. Park, not kill: the franchise is not impaired, it is out-scaled, and it is one of very few universe names that gains from disorder. The memo adopts rather than overrides the Risks report's own hold-and-watch recommendation. Richard decides at the Friday review meeting.
case: The memo's spine is a single judgement: Flow Traders is a wasting long-volatility option. The convexity is genuine, but the strike price is falling at roughly 20% a year on revenue capture and 170 basis points a quarter on European share. An investor is paid for the spike and pays for the wait, and the wait now has a named cost.

Step one, the change forces are large but badly signed. The external backdrop is the best in the firm's history and is measured rather than projected: assets up 41% year-on-year to EUR 20.2 trillion, value traded up 33% year-on-year in 2Q26 and 73% in 1Q26, non-bank trading firms projected to take 30% of global trading volumes by 2030 from 20% in 2025, tokenised real-world assets up from $22bn to $34bn in six months, and a crypto-asset regime that delivered a BaFin electronic-money licence through the AllUnity venture with DWS and Galaxy for the first fully compliant euro stablecoin. The internal change forces are equally real in form: an external chief executive from November 2025, a genuine strategy reset in Horizon 2030 with a public admission that the firm "spread ourselves too thin and delivered on too few", a 75% balance-sheet expansion since 2Q24, a rebuilt Asia-Pacific leadership, and a technology reset going live in 2027.

Step two, the transmission from those forces to earnings is broken, and one datapoint proves it. European share kept falling while dollar trading capital rose 90% and average volatility rose. That is precisely the test that separates a capital-starvation story from a competitive-displacement story, and it removes management's own explanation. The memo applies the Red Queen Effect model from the Wisdom Library: a firm spending 90% more capital to hold a falling share is running to stand still, which is the model's definition of a treadmill disguised as a compounder. The same failure repeats regionally: Asia-Pacific market value traded doubled in 1H26 while Flow's regional value traded fell 1%, attributed to infrastructure and licensing delays.
counter_case: The strongest version of the bull case is stated in the memo in full, not in caricature.

Convexity is real and historically evidenced. A single quarter of genuine dislocation previously produced EUR 495m of net trading income, more than three times the most recent quarter, on a business now carrying 38% more capital. The gearing works both ways, with 3Q25 net trading income of EUR 78.3m when average volatility fell to 15.97, so the payoff is convex rather than linear. Jefferies estimates every 10% decline in volatility cuts base earnings per share by about 8%. In portfolio terms this is the attribute that makes the name interesting at all: a concentrated long-only book of 12 to 20 positions has no other asset that gains from dislocation.
triggers: Progression tests, any two of three at the FY26 results in early 2027: European exchange-traded-product share at or above 27% with sequential quarterly gains, which is the Risks report's own progression threshold and the sharpest single discriminator; annualised return on trading capital above 60% across two consecutive quarters, proving marginal capital deployment earns rather than dilutes; fixed operating expenses inside EUR 235m to 245m with FY27 guidance below EUR 250m, proving the cost step is a step and not a slope.

Fastest single mind-changer: one quarter showing European share up sequentially with revenue capture stable, since that pairing falsifies the structural reading directly. Two consecutive quarters of share gain in a low-volatility regime would revive the cyclical counter-argument.
Invalidation of the park itself: a sustained volatility regime above the mid-twenties on the volatility index would re-rate earnings faster than the memo's tests can be read.

Monitorables carried from the Risks report: European share below 25% alongside revenue capture under 2.3 basis points flags simultaneous competitive and yield failure; fixed costs above EUR 240m with return on trading capital below 40% confirms operating-leverage inversion. Memo-set monitors: revenue capture quarterly against the 2.0 basis-point warning threshold; net liquidity posted at clearing houses and prime brokers as the leading indicator of supplier extraction; a standing false-friend monitor pairing value traded against revenue capture and trading capital against return on trading capital each quarter; a standing change-from-current item count required to fall below five before progression is reconsidered.

Key questions for any future Early-Stage Assessment: whether revenue capture stabilises above 2.3 basis points; whether Asia-Pacific converts market growth into company volume; whether the deep-learning division produces measurable spread capture. Research gaps logged but not run, Triaging carrying a zero bespoke-research mandate: expert calls with institutional fund issuers on whether request-for-quote flow is genuinely diverting to better-capitalised market makers, and with former crypto over-the-counter traders on altcoin spread compression and the cost of having no in-house custody.

Portfolio question that precedes the stock question: whether a long-volatility equity hedge is wanted in a 12 to 20 position book at all. A park verdict is not a hedge decision, and a low Triaging grade is not an argument against holding portfolio volatility protection by another instrument.
